title: Daily routine and small talk
lead: Is lesson ke baad tum Monday morning chat, lunch break aur weekend plans par 2–3 minute English small talk kar paoge — bina Hindi switch kiye.
description: Week 2 English lesson: daily routine, weekend small talk, present simple, past simple, and follow-up questions.

patterns.note: Usually + verb; time ke pehle at.
patterns.say: I usually check my email at nine.
patterns.positive: I usually check my email at nine.
patterns.negative: I don't usually check email at night.
patterns.question: What do you usually do in the morning?
examples: I usually start work at ten.
Main aam taur par das baje kaam shuru karta hoon.
She usually takes the metro to the office.
Woh aam taur par office metro se jaati hai.
patterns.grammar: Present simple + frequency adverb. usually/always/often/sometimes/never verb se pehle aate hain: I usually work. am/is/are ke baad: I'm usually busy.
patterns.mistake: “I am usually go to office at 10” → “I usually go to office at 10.” Usually ke saath base verb.

patterns.note: Negative habit; very often = bahut zyada baar nahi.
patterns.say: I don't watch cricket very often.
patterns.positive: I watch cricket almost every weekend.
patterns.negative: I don't watch cricket very often.
patterns.question: Do you watch cricket very often?
examples: I don't go to the gym very often.
Main bahut zyada baar gym nahi jaata.
We don't eat out very often.
Hum bahut zyada baar bahar nahi khaate.
patterns.grammar: don't/doesn't + base verb. very often sentence ke end me. Not very often = rarely.
patterns.mistake: “I don't watched cricket” → “I don't watch cricket.” don't ke baad base verb.

patterns.note: Weekend khatam ho gaya, isliye was. Aaj ke liye How is your day?
patterns.question: How was your weekend?
examples: It was busy, but I enjoyed it.
Vyast tha, lekin maza aaya.
My weekend was quiet. I stayed home.
Mera weekend shaant tha. Main ghar par ruka.
patterns.grammar: Past simple be: was/were. Weekend singular → was; days/events plural → were.
patterns.mistake: “How is your weekend?” (Monday ko) → “How was your weekend?” Weekend past me khatam ho gaya.

patterns.note: went = go ka past; stayed = ghar ya kisi jagah ruka.
patterns.say: I went to my cousin's place and stayed there for two hours.
patterns.positive: I went to my cousin's place and stayed there for two hours.
patterns.negative: I didn't go out on Sunday.
patterns.question: Where did you go on Sunday?
examples: I went to the market in the morning.
Main subah market gaya.
We stayed home and watched a movie.
Hum ghar par ruke aur movie dekhi.
patterns.grammar: Past simple irregular: go → went. stay → stayed. ghar ke liye: I stayed home / I stayed at home.
patterns.mistake: “I went to home” → “I went home.” Home ke pehle to nahi lagta.

patterns.note: Like ke baad noun ya verb+ing.
patterns.say: Do you like working from home?
patterns.negative: I don't like waking up early.
patterns.question: Do you like working from home?
examples: Do you like tea or coffee?
Aapko chai pasand hai ya coffee?
I like watching movies on Sunday.
Mujhe Sunday ko movie dekhna pasand hai.
patterns.grammar: like + noun / verb-ing. Short answer: Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
patterns.mistake: “Do you like work from home?” → “Do you like working from home?” Like ke baad verb-ing.

patterns.note: Same question wapas poochhne ka short tarika.
patterns.say: I'm a developer. What about you?
patterns.positive: I'm a developer. What about you?
patterns.negative: I'm not very busy today. What about you?
patterns.question: What about you?
examples: I usually commute by bike. What about you?
Main aam taur par bike se jaata hoon. Tum?
I like cricket. What about you?
Mujhe cricket pasand hai. Tumhe?
patterns.grammar: What about you? = And you? Same topic continue karta hai. Formal me And you? bhi chalega.
patterns.mistake: “What about your?” → “What about you?” You subject aur object dono me same rehta hai.

grammarRules: I don't watch TV very often.
It was good. I went home.
Questions: Do you + base verb? / How was ___?
Do you like tea? How was your weekend?
mistakes: I am usually go to office at 10.
I usually go to office at 10.
Frequency adverb ke baad base verb.
Weekend past me khatam ho gaya, isliye was.
Home ke pehle to nahi lagta.
Do you like work from home?
Do you like working from home?
You subject aur object dono me same rehta hai.

speakPrompts.title: 1. Your morning routine
speakPrompts.prompt: Subah se office tak 4 lines bolo.
speakPrompts.starter: I usually wake up at ___ . I ___ at ___ . I usually start work at ___ .

speakPrompts.title: 2. Your weekend
speakPrompts.prompt: Last weekend kya kiya, past simple me bolo.
speakPrompts.starter: My weekend was ___ . I went to ___ . I stayed ___ .

speakPrompts.title: 3. Ask them back
speakPrompts.starter: How was your weekend? Do you like ___ ? What about you?

speakPrompts.title: 4. Two-minute chat
speakPrompts.prompt: Friend ke saath 2 minute conversation record karo.
speakPrompts.starter: Hi! How are you? ... What about you? ... Do you like ___ ?

vocab.example: I have a simple morning routine.
I slept a lot over the weekend.
I spend Sunday with my family.
We watched a movie on Sunday.
I don't watch cricket very often.
I go to the gym three times a week.
There was heavy traffic this morning.
I don't get enough sleep on weekdays.

selfCheck: Apna morning routine 3 lines me bola.
Last weekend ke baare me past simple (was/went/stayed) use kiya.
“I usually ___” aur “I don't ___ very often” use kiya.
Ek question wapas poochha — “What about you?”
2 minute tak English me bola, Hindi minimum thi.
went, stayed aur was ka pronunciation clear tha.

pronunciation.title: -s endings
pronunciation.body: works = work + /s/; watches = watch + /ɪz/; goes = go + /z/. Practice: works, lives, watches.

pronunciation.title: Sentence rhythm
pronunciation.body: Content words par stress: I USUALLY START WORK at TEN. usually/at ko halka bolo.

pronunciation.title: was / were
pronunciation.body: was = /wɒz/ short; were = /wɜːr/. “It was good” me was ko lamba mat karo.

pronunciation.title: went
pronunciation.body: went = /went/, final /t/ clear. “I went home” ko “I wen home” mat bolo.

followUps: Mera “usually” sentence me sahi position par hai?
“How was your weekend?” ka natural reply kya hoga?
Meri recording me kaunsa word clear nahi tha?
Small talk me aur kaunse safe questions poochh sakta hoon?
“I went to my cousin's place” natural lagta hai?
mission: Ek colleague se ek real small-talk question English me poochho — “How was your weekend?” ya “Do you like ___?” — aur uska answer suno.
